title: Cleaning, maintenance and records
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: cleaning, maintenance and records

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning goal and job context: This lesson teaches cleaning, maintenance and records for routine cleaning work. Start with the actual job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and worker training. Never treat a general lesson as authority to perform restricted or specialist work.

Core procedure: After work, remove soil safely, clean and dry reusable tools, empty tanks by the authorised route, inspect filters and replace consumables. Segregate contaminated tools for reprocessing. Record damage, service dates and outstanding faults; return only serviceable equipment to clean storage.

Decision-making in the field: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

Worked workplace scenario: A wet mop is left sealed in a bucket overnight. The team identifies contamination risk and changes the drying and storage process.

Guided supervised practice: Complete an end-of-shift equipment turnaround, fault log and storage audit.

Evidence and feedback: The assessor observes the task and checks whether the learner: equipment is clean, dry, correctly stored and traceable for maintenance. A learner must explain any unsafe choice, correct it and repeat the demonstration. Record observations, required coaching and reassessment rather than awarding competence from attendance alone.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Remove soil from equipment safely at the end of the job.
Clean and dry reusable tools before they go back into storage.
Empty tanks only by the route the site authorises.
Inspect filters and replace consumables as the manufacturer's directions and site instructions require.
Segregate contaminated tools for reprocessing, and keep them apart from clean equipment.
Record damage, service dates and outstanding faults.
Return only serviceable equipment to clean storage, and keep it traceable for maintenance.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

qualityStandard: Reusable tools are cleaned and dried after work, and tanks are emptied by the authorised route.
Contaminated tools are segregated for reprocessing.
Damage, service dates and outstanding faults are recorded.
Only serviceable equipment is returned to clean storage, and the equipment is traceable for maintenance.
summary: After work, soil is removed safely, reusable tools are cleaned and dried, tanks are emptied by the authorised route, and filters and consumables are inspected or replaced.
Contaminated tools are segregated for reprocessing, and damage, service dates and outstanding faults are recorded.
Only serviceable equipment goes back into clean storage.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before ending a job with cleaning, maintenance and records?
options: That tools are left wet in a sealed bucket overnight until the next visit and the bucket lid stays on
That contaminated tools are used again before reprocessing and the bucket is put back in the store with the others
That tools are clean and dry, tanks are emptied by the authorised route, and the fault record is updated
That a fault may be left unrecorded if the machine still runs and the next shift can deal with it

knowledgeChecks.question: When can equipment with a recorded fault go back into storage?
options: Store it with clean equipment and fix it at the next clean and the fault is left for the next team
Use it for one more job, since it is nearly fine and the fault is small and will not spread
Ask a colleague to sign off the fault without an inspection and then put it back in storage
Remove it from service, segregate and record the fault, and return it to storage only when serviceable
